sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Polk County, NC?
sections.html:
Deeds for Polk County land are recorded at the Polk County Register of Deeds, 40 Courthouse St., Columbus, NC 28722. The mailing address is PO Box 308, the county lists hours of 8:30 to 5:00, Monday through Friday, and the phone is (828) 894-8450.

The county describes the office's job as recording deeds, powers of attorney, cancellations of deeds of trust and plats. It also keeps marriage, birth and death records and files assumed business names. For a home seller, the first group is what counts, because a sale is not complete in the public record until the deed is in these books.

sections.h2: What does a recorded deed change for Polk County property taxes?
sections.html:
Once a deed is recorded, the Polk County tax records are updated to match. The county's ownership and transfer page says a plat recorded at the same office also triggers an update to tax and mapping records.

Timing matters, though. The county states that, for tax purposes, ownership is set as of January 1 each year, and the owner of record on that date carries the liability for the year if the property sells later. Any split of the bill between seller and buyer is a private agreement, and the county sends such questions to the closing attorney or the agent. Keep your mailing address current so bills and assessment notices reach you.

sections.h2: How is Polk County's parcel data kept current after a sale?
sections.html:
Parcel information on the county's GIS site is refreshed every one to two months. If you sold or bought within the last two months and the map still shows the old name, the Register of Deeds page tells you to call the tax office at (828) 894-8954.

  • Record the deed first; the tax records follow the recording.
  • Check the GIS site a few weeks later for the new owner name.
  • Call the tax office if the old name persists after two months.
  • Send the new owner's mailing address to the tax office so the next bill goes to the right place.

The county's ownership and transfer page lists (828) 894-8500 for questions about ownership and transfers.

sections.h2: What does the state charge to record in Polk County?
sections.html:
Recording fees are uniform across North Carolina, and the figures sit in G.S. 161-10. The Polk County page itself does not print a fee schedule, so the table below comes from the statute. Call the register's office to confirm the total for your document.

Recording fees printed in G.S. 161-10, which apply in Polk County
DocumentFee
Instruments in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 each extra page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, $4.00 each extra page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each extra page

A non-standard document adds $25.00 and extra instruments in one filing add $10.00 each, per the same statute. Fees are collected before the document is filed.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Polk County deed?
sections.html:
The seller does. The statute, G.S. 105-228.30, sets the tax at $1.00 for each $500, or fraction of $500, of the price or value conveyed, and says the transferor pays the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

Half of the receipts go to the county general fund and the other half goes to the State. In a Polk County sale the figure appears on the settlement statement. Ask the closing attorney to show how it was figured from the price.

sections.h2: Why does recording time matter when you sell in Polk County?
sections.html:
North Carolina's recording statute, G.S. 47-18, makes a conveyance or option effective against lien creditors and paying purchasers only from registration in the county where the land lies. Priority follows order of registration.

That means two things for you. First, a deed from a family member or a previous sale that was never recorded should be recorded before you sell. Second, a released loan only clears title when the lender records its cancellation. Polk County offers a Property Check sign-up on its Register of Deeds page, which alerts owners when something is recorded against their name. It is worth using whenever a house sits vacant or is part of an estate.

sections.h2: Does a contract for deed need to be recorded in North Carolina?
sections.html:
Yes, in a way. Chapter 47H covers seller-financed purchases of one to four family homes, and it requires the seller to record the contract, or a short memorandum of it, within five business days. The buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing.

If you sell on a contract for deed, or you bought that way, the recording step protects both sides, and the register of deeds office is where it happens. The chapter also sets a cure period of at least 30 days in a written default notice before any forfeiture. Have an attorney read the contract first.

sections.h2: What does the Polk County register not handle?
sections.html:
Three nearby offices cover what this one does not. The tax office sets values and sends bills. The clerk of superior court handles estate filings and foreclosure hearings. A closing attorney or title company handles title searches and the settlement.

State law puts a small-estate affidavit with the clerk of court in the county where the person lived, and the affidavit must describe each tract of land the person owned. Once the court side is finished, the deed or other papers that move the land are what the register of deeds records. For an inherited Polk County house, plan on both offices, starting with the clerk.

Foreclosure also runs through the clerk. The sale itself is a power-of-sale hearing before the clerk in the county where the land lies, with an upset bid period afterward, and the buyer's deed is recorded here afterward.

sections.h2: How should a Polk County seller handle taxes and recording at closing?
sections.html:
Treat them as two separate tracks with one office each. The Register of Deeds records the deed and collects the transfer tax. The tax office handles the bill.

State law, G.S. 105-360, makes taxes due September 1, payable at face value through January 5, with interest starting January 6. Because Polk County fixes liability to the January 1 owner, ask the closing attorney who is paying the current bill and how it is split. Ask the Polk County tax office for the balance and rate.

If a house is inherited, vacant, rented or needs repairs, a cash purchase can shorten the schedule. The deed recording steps above do not change with the type of buyer.

faqs.q: What are the Polk County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The county lists 8:30 to 5:00, Monday through Friday, at 40 Courthouse St. in Columbus. Call (828) 894-8450 before you go, since holidays can change the schedule.

faqs.q: Does Polk County update tax records after a deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says tax records are updated once a deed is recorded at the Register of Deeds. Parcel data on the GIS site refreshes every one to two months.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the current year's tax if I sell mid-year?
faqs.a: The county says ownership for tax purposes is fixed as of January 1, so the January 1 owner carries the liability. Any split with the buyer is a private contract handled at closing.

faqs.q: How much is the North Carolina excise tax on a deed?
faqs.a: It is $1.00 for each $500 or fraction of $500 of the price or value, paid by the seller to the register of deeds before recording, under G.S. 105-228.30.

faqs.q: Does recording a mortgage release cost anything in Polk County?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 lists no fee for recording satisfactions or cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages. Make sure your lender actually files the release.
